sampling_model.design: Observational independent sampling from an unknown discrete-confounder law with fixed known overlap constant \(\epsilon\).
sampling_model.overlap: Null cells are permitted; positivity is imposed only when \(p_k>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cell masses, propensities, and arm means are unknown. Estimators may use the known inputs \(n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma\), must guard every denominator, and must return a value for every sample.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 2--4 establish binary-outcome unrestricted and exact-homogeneity rates, while Section 4.2 leaves intermediate maximal-radius dependence open.
The accepted same-class parent proves lower rate \(b_{n,d}+\sigma^2\min\{1,u_{n,d}\}\) and upper rate \(n^{-1}+\min\{1,u_{n,d},\sigma^2+d/n^2\}\).
A chi-square functional modulus is dual to a bias--variance optimization under convexity and compactness conditions.
Heavy--light polynomial estimation matches moment-based converses for separable large-alphabet functionals.

body.tldr: The kernel is the finite-sample minimax MSE frontier for an identified ATE when high-dimensional discrete adjustment cells have effects within a calibrated maximal radius \(\sigma M\) of the ATE.  The exact split-sample empirical-mass estimator gives collision-scale risk \(M^2/n\) for \(2\le d\le n\) when \(\sigma^2d^2\le n\), while the inherited rare-cell approximation branch gives the same rate when \(u_{n,d}\le n^{-1}\), equivalently \(d^2\le n\log^2(en)\).  Thus approximate common effects retain collision-scale estimation on the union of these two directly checkable regions.  At the still-unresolved benchmark \(d=n\), \(\sigma^2=\log^2(en)/n\), an exactly normalized shared-design marked family fails because its global outcome shift makes the full mixtures distinguishable; the conditionally centered marked-coupling repair remains open, and no global frontier formula is asserted.

project_justification.gap: The closest published work gives the binary-outcome unrestricted and exact-homogeneity endpoints and explicitly leaves maximal-radius dependence unresolved.  The accepted same-class parent gives a nonmatching bracket; the present results close the additional union \(\sigma^2d^2\le n\) or \(d^2\le n\log^2(en)\) for \(d\le n\), but not the remaining radius-dependent wedge.
project_justification.niche: Unknown random cell masses, unknown overlapping propensities, empty cells, supportwise centering around the ATE, and only conditional second moments make the residual converse neither fixed-design shrinkage nor a routine polynomial-functional problem.  The corrected residual wedge additionally enforces \(u_{n,d}>n^{-1}\), so already-closed approximation-scale points are excluded.
project_justification.fill: The project gives a total empirical-mass estimator, proves collision-scale minimax risk on the union of the empirical and rare-cell approximation regions, and proves a full-mixture obstruction for the displayed benchmark prior.  For lower-bound transfer, the published binary anchor embeds in the present real-outcome class through \(Y'=M(Y-1/2)\), which scales ATEs and squared risks by \(M\) and \(M^2\).  For the real-outcome upper bound, the declared envelopes imply \(E_P[Y^2\mid A=a,X=k]\le v_{ak}+\mu_{ak}^2\le5M^2/4\).  The precisely specified conditionally centered shared-design converse remains open.

body.related_work: Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy (2024, revised 2026) provide the binary-outcome baseline in Theorems 2--4; Section 4.2 identifies the unresolved radius dependence and discusses extension under bounded conditional second moments.  Their binary anchor transfers into the present centered real-outcome class by \(Y'=M(Y-1/2)\): conditional means then lie in \([-M/2,M/2]\), conditional central variances are at most \(M^2/4\), ATE separations scale by \(M\), and squared-error lower bounds scale by \(M^2\).  Conversely, the real-outcome upper analysis uses only \(E_P[Y^2\mid A=a,X=k]\le v_{ak}+\mu_{ak}^2\le5M^2/4\), not bounded outcomes.  Section 7's 401(k) eligibility and net-assets analysis is the consumer but does not validate overlap or its reported intervals.  The internal accepted parent supplies the same-class bracket and the channel and factorial-lift obstructions.  The approximation and mixture architectures are informed by Zeng et al.'s cited polynomial-functional literature, but none of those sources resolves exact normalization, self-centering, or supportwise radius here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: A hypothesis-independent outcome-channel transfer gives only product-scale separation, and the natural centered linear Chebyshev factorial lift has excessive singleton-pair variance even with oracle centering at \(\sigma=0\).  The explicit family \(\Pi_h^\star\) further shows that exact normalization, identical design marginals, supportwise radius, and separated ATEs are not sufficient: its hypothesis-wide outcome shift yields a sign test with total variation tending to one at \(d=n\) and \(\sigma^2=\log^2(en)/n\).  The newly closed approximation branch removes every \(d\le n\) point with \(u_{n,d}\le n^{-1}\) from the residual problem.  Any replacement converse must operate in the corrected wedge, eliminate the globally visible first-order coefficient, and control the full marked likelihood.
body.honest_scope: Consistency and exchangeability identify the displayed ATE.  The established claims are the empirical-mass risk bound, the refined infimum-risk bracket, collision-scale minimax risk for \(2\le d\le n\) whenever \(\sigma^2d^2\le n\) or \(u_{n,d}\le n^{-1}\), and failure of the displayed benchmark global-shift prior.  The open domain \(\mathcal W\) now requires \(n^{-1}<u_{n,d}<1\) in addition to \(d>n\) or \(\sigma^2d^2>n\); the benchmark marked-prior repair remains open inside that domain.  No global sharp rate, unspecified selector, unknown-radius adaptation, confidence interval, bounded-outcome assumption, overlap validation, or claim about the reported 401(k) intervals is included.
